newsitem.title: USA: Edison International endorses Calif. bill.
newsitem.headline: Edison International endorses Calif. bill.

text.p: Edison International's Southern California Edison says it supports the California Assembly bill which would dramatically restructure the state's electric industry.
The bill cleared a key conference committee on Tuesday and could be voted on by the full State Legislature as early as Friday.

"This process has been a model of consensus building and compromise," said Edison chairman chief executive officer John Bryson, noting that the bill "ensures a timely and fair transition to a competitive electricity market."

Edison said the proposed bill would open electric power generation in California to competition while leaving in place the regulated system of transmission and distribution of power. It expects this new, competitive generation market to contribute to lowering electric rates for all consumers.

"We believe the Legislature has given us a fair opportunity to recover stranded costs, although we recognize that we are at risk to complete recovery of Edison generation costs under the rate freeze and within the specified transition periods," said Bryson.

Other publicly-owned electric utilities operating in California include Pacific Gas and Electric Co , PacifiCorp, San Diego Gas & Electric Co, Sierra Pacific Resources Corp and Southern California Water Co.
